current.text: He joined the Lakers from Utah and is locked in as their starting center.
The Lakers' backup centers are weak (Kevon Looney, with Mamukelashvili likely taking those minutes), and the team defense depends heavily on Kessler.
With weak backups behind him, he should play a lot of minutes.
Playing with Luka Doncic should give him plenty of rebounds, pick and roll chances and easy finishes as a roller and dunker.
Expected line: about 12 to 15 points (around six off offensive rebounds), double-digit rebounds, 2 or more blocks and bad free throws.
Last season's shoulder injury needed surgery but is not a concern now. Experts say not to avoid him over the missed games; he might play 80.
His jumps in threes, steals, assists and free throw shooting last season came from a five-game sample (75% from three, inflated steal rate). Experts do not expect them to last.
If those steals, threes and assists do not hold, he is not a top 70 player in category leagues.
His draft spot varies a lot, from early round 3 to late round 4 in mock drafts.

Experts call him overpriced at his Yahoo rank of about 38 and in rounds 2 to 3. Around 60th overall is fair. Do not draft him before round 4; one expert would not take him in round 4 either and calls him his biggest fade.
In an auction mock, one expert would pay no more than 15 USD for him. He went for 26 USD.
At ESPN's lower price (ADP around 80) he is a fine pick.
The Lakers have the second most back-to-backs in the league, which raises the risk of soft tissue injuries.
The Lakers' playoff schedule with a March 28 end is 3-4-3 games, in the bottom half of the league.

durable.text: He is a rebounds, blocks and FG% center. Those three categories are clear league outliers.
He is a very one-dimensional player. He is below average in points, threes, assists and steals, and his free throws hurt a team's FT%.
He has a 20 to 25% career three-point percentage.
He is an elite rim protector and defensive rebounder, though he may not be able to carry a whole defense the way Rudy Gobert did.
He has had arm or shoulder problems in two of the last three seasons, including shoulder surgery after five games last season. It is unclear how many minutes his body can handle.

note: He is a clear rebounds, blocks and FG% anchor whose FT% (about 59%) makes him a natural punt FT% center. Experts agree he is overpriced at Yahoo (rank 38, value 25 USD, average cost 17 USD) and put fair value around 60th overall, closer to ESPN's 12 USD and the 15 USD he cost in our league last season, so do not go much past 15 USD. Early in the season, check whether last season's threes and steals were real (projections say no), how many minutes his shoulder handles, and note that the Lakers have many back-to-backs and a below-average playoff schedule.
